experiment: Independent three-tube axisymmetric CFD blood, frozen biochemical transfer
reference: ALE axisymmetric Navier-Stokes in each tube, monolithic common-normal-traction and net-flux junction; resolved chemical transport with perfect mixing at junction
baseline: Fixed C0 from three-vessel-method-lock-v1; unchanged equations, mesh, D, rate, boundary conventions
primary_blood: Independent CFD, identical A/Q for C0 and all frozen networks
secondary_blood: Original Sen projected A/Q, identical for C0 and all frozen networks; evaluate against exactly the same independent chemical targets and observations
reference_inlets: Same fixed 48-amplitude archive; computing the first 24 again does not constitute training
metric: Per-case space-time volume-weighted relative L2, using independent CFD reference volumes for both methods and both blood inputs; average cases, then seeds

inverse.selection: Locked previous validation choices; no new tuning on independent CFD test data

isolation: Both blood arms use the same checkpoints, observations, noise, regularization, starting rule and stopping criteria. Paired change is total impact of replacing blood fields, not an additive error identity.
interpretation: Sen-vs-independent-CFD blood discrepancy includes original 1D-vs-axisymmetric physics and neural reconstruction error; a separate Sen-vs-raw-1D table isolates reconstruction against its source.
limitations: No bifurcation angle or junction recirculation
Synthetic biochemical kinetics and inlet ensemble, not measured coagulation
